statement: The first line holds n and m - nodes 0 to n-1 and undirected edges. The next m lines each hold an edge. Print yes when the nodes can be split into two camps such that every edge joins the camps, and no otherwise. Two-colour during a BFS or DFS: colour each newly discovered node opposite to its discoverer; when a walk meets an already-coloured neighbour wearing the same colour, an odd cycle exists and the split is impossible. Walk every component - the graph may be disconnected.

example.why: The square alternates camps cleanly: nodes 0 and 2 against nodes 1 and 3.

hint: Three states per node: uncoloured, camp 0, camp 1 - and the clash test runs on every edge.
mistake: Colouring a fresh component with the leftover colour variable instead of starting it at camp 0 deliberately.
